note: Window agent p1760-p1769 (phase D, 2 Nov 2026). Five entries: Rupert's Land keeps the Red River/Souris basins (2 rulings); the Sikh misls keep Lahore and Amritsar from April 1765 (1 event); Yedisan stays Ottoman in 1769 (2 keyframe overrides, which also reach 1770-1771 of the next window).

region.text: the Bhangi misl's country: 'The Bhangis held the Upper Rechna Doab, Upper Chajj Doab, and territory around Lahore and Amritsar' (Cliopatria's Sikh Confederacy shape)

events.note: 16 April 1765: 'the Bhangi sardars Gujjar Singh and Lehna Singh Kahlon, allied with Sobha Singh of the Kanhaiya Misl, conquered Lahore.' The page puts Lahore and Amritsar in the Bhangi territory and mentions no Durrani recapture in 1766-1767. The dossier's own sikh-confederacy_1765 keyframe already gives the misls this land, but the same-year contest_end (events/4) hands the whole contested Punjab back to the Durrani and the keyframe only wins in 1769 (215 cells snapped then). This event moves the land in April 1765 itself.

union.text: Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts: Yedisan, the Black Sea steppe round Hadjibey (Odesa) and Ozu (Ochakiv), Ottoman Ozu eyalet land held through the Nogai Horde, with the land east of the Southern Bug (ceded only after the 1768-1774 war) and the Budjak coast west of the Dniester (Ottoman in 1762-1768; no opened page dates a Russian gain there in 1769)

minus.text: occupied Moldavia (carried by the occupation events), Ottoman Yedisan and the Budjak coast

correction.text: the 1769 shape without occupied Moldavia and without Ottoman Yedisan and the Budjak coast (Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts)

keyframe_overrides.why: Yedisan was 'placed by the Ottomans under the control of the Nogai Horde', part of the Silistra (Ozu) Eyalet with 'Khadjibey (Odesa) and Ozu (Ochakiv) as major centers'; only after the 1768-1774 war did 'the Ottomans ceded to Russia the region east of the Southern Bug', and the takeover was complete only with the Treaty of Jassy (1792). The 1769 shape (133 cells of Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts snapped from the Ottoman Empire) gives Russia land it did not hold. The shape runs 1769-1771, so 1770-1771 of the next window are affected. Odesa oblast also holds the Budjak west of the Dniester (about 46 of these cells), which the Yedisan page does not name: it stays Ottoman as in 1762-1768, since the Russo-Turkish War (1768-1774) page dates the campaign only from 17 September 1769, when 'the Russians began their initial campaign over the Dniester into Moldavia' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1768%E2%80%931774)), and the dossier's own note treats Moldavia and Bessarabia as occupation, not Russian land. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: texts amended for the Budjak; the region spec is unchanged.]

union.text: Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts: Yedisan, the Black Sea steppe round Hadjibey (Odesa) and Ozu (Ochakiv), Ottoman Ozu eyalet land held through the Nogai Horde, with the land east of the Southern Bug (ceded only after the 1768-1774 war) and the Budjak coast west of the Dniester (Ottoman in 1762-1768; no opened page dates a Russian gain there in 1769)

minus.text: Cliopatria's 1769 shape plus Ottoman Yedisan and the Budjak coast

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape plus Yedisan and the Budjak coast (Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts), without Azov, ceded to Russia in 1739

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1769 Ottoman shape drops Odesa and Mykolaiv oblasts, but Yedisan was Ottoman (Nogai-held, Ozu Eyalet) until the east-of-the-Bug cession after the 1768-1774 war and the whole of it until 1792; the Russian keyframe override above stops the Russian claim, and this one keeps the land Ottoman. Azov stays out as in the dossier. The shape runs 1769-1771. The spec also keeps the Budjak west of the Dniester Ottoman (as in 1762-1768; no opened page dates a change in 1769) and adds about 30 cells that were nobody's in 1762-1768, most of them east of the Southern Bug in Mykolaiv oblast: the Ottomans 'ceded to Russia the region east of the Southern Bug' only after the war, and by the 1774 treaty 'Russia gained the territory between the rivers Dnieper and Southern Bug' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1768%E2%80%931774)). [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: texts amended; the region spec is unchanged.]

union.text: North Dakota east of the Missouri Coteau divide: the Red River valley, Devils Lake and Souris basins (the researcher's reading of the drainage divide; the Missouri-drained west and south of the state are left out)
northwestern Minnesota, the Red River and Rainy River side (the researcher's reading, as in rupert-s-land)

region.text: the Hudson Bay drainage south of 49 N (Red River valley, Devils Lake and Souris basins of North Dakota and northwestern Minnesota)

rulings.why: The Rupert's Land page says it 'extended into areas that are now parts of Minnesota, North Dakota, and Montana' and that its southern border 'west of Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains was the drainage divide between the Mississippi and Red/Saskatchewan watersheds until the Anglo-American Convention of 1818'; the Louisiana (New Spain) page says 'The territorial boundaries had not been defined in the Treaty of Fontainebleau'. The size rule gave the Red River and Souris basins to Spanish Louisiana in 1762 and the keyframe then set them to nobody.
